name: gizza-ai/weighted-random-sampler
summary: Draw a weighted random sample of rows from a CSV or JSON dataset, with or without replacement

tool.description: Draw a weighted random sample of `n` rows from a CSV or JSON-array dataset. Each row is selected with probability proportional to a numeric `weight_field` (CSV header name / 1-based index, or JSON object key). `replacement=true` allows a row to be drawn more than once and lets `n` exceed the row count; `replacement=false` (default) draws each row at most once (capped at the positive-weight rows) and preserves the input order. Draws are reproducible via `seed`. The output is emitted in the same `format` as the input; for CSV the header and `delimiter` are preserved.

data.description: The dataset to sample from — CSV text (with header by default) or a JSON array of objects, matching `format`.

delimiter.description: CSV only: field delimiter of the input, also used for the output. Ignored for JSON. Default comma.

format.description: Input/output format: csv (delimited rows) or json (an array of objects). The result is emitted in the same format. Default csv.

header.description: CSV only: treat the first row as a header (kept in the output and used to resolve a named weight_field). Ignored for JSON. Default true.

n.description: Number of rows to draw. Without replacement it is capped at the count of positive-weight rows (error if larger); with replacement it may exceed the row count. Default 2.

replacement.description: Sample WITH replacement (a row may be drawn more than once) when true; WITHOUT replacement (each row at most once, output in original order) when false. Default false.

seed.description: Seed for the reproducible PRNG. The same seed + inputs always yields the same draw; change it for a different sample. Default 42.

weight_field.description: Field holding each row's weight. For CSV: a header name (header=true) or a 1-based column index. For JSON: the object key. Weights must be non-negative numbers; higher weight = more likely to be drawn.
